channel.title: MCP on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in MCP on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: github: Agentic CLI customizations now in the usage metrics API
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s usage metrics API now includes agentic CLI activity for skills, custom agents, MCP servers, slash commands, and plugins. This extends existing CLI report coverage with additional customization metrics.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: PostgreSQL skills and MCP plugin for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
item.description:
Microsoft previewed PostgreSQL skills and an MCP plugin for Azure Database for PostgreSQL. The plugin is intended to make supported AI coding assistants context-aware for PostgreSQL and able to provide guidance and perform actions on a connected database.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: How Uno Platform uses .NET, MCP, and AI to build high quality apps
item.description:
Uno Platform built two MCP servers in C# to let AI agents use real documentation as context and interact with a running cross-platform .NET app. The post describes how .NET, MCP, and AI are combined to support app development and validation.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot app Customize tab is generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s new Customize tab in the Copilot app is now generally available. It is meant to connect Copilot with a team’s existing tools, knowledge, and workflows, including MCP.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise managed settings in GitHub Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now supports enterprise managed settings. Administrators can centrally control plugin governance, MCP server access, OpenTelemetry, and permission modes across the enterprise.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: From single call to agents: five new Claude capabilities now available in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now supports five new Claude capabilities on Azure-hosted models: structured outputs, web search, web fetch, MCP connector, and tool search. The update positions a model endpoint for agent-style workflows rather than single-call usage.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: Copilot memory and Ollama in GitHub Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains adds persistent memory, local model access via Ollama, and additional enterprise controls. The update also improves chat workflows and fixes reliability issues with MCP servers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: MCP allowlists in enterprise managed settings
item.description:
GitHub added enterprise-managed settings to centrally control which MCP servers GitHub Copilot clients can run. Enterprise owners can now use allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers to allowlist or block specific MCP servers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: Agent skills and MCP now generally available
item.description:
Copilot code review now generally supports agent skills and MCP servers for all Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business, and Enterprise users. These features have moved from public preview to general availability.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Announcing v2.0 of the official MCP C# SDK
item.description:
The official MCP C# SDK v2.0 now implements the 2026-07-28 MCP specification. It adds a stateless-first protocol, standardized HTTP headers, and Multi Round-Trip Requests for interactive tools while remaining backward compatible.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains adds improved OpenTelemetry configuration and model management
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now includes improved OpenTelemetry configuration and model management. The update also adds support for connecting MCP servers and custom agents in Claude agent flows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Analyze MSBuild Binary Logs with Copilot in VS Code
item.description:
Microsoft introduced the MSBuild Binlog Analyzer for VS Code, a Copilot-powered tool for reading MSBuild binary logs, explaining build failures, suggesting fixes, comparing builds, and identifying regressions. It uses the Microsoft.AITools.BinlogMcp MCP server.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: GitHub MCP Server supports the next MCP specification
item.description:
GitHub MCP Server will support the upcoming MCP spec ahead of its official release. The key protocol change is a move to a stateless core on 28 July 2026.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Building Agents that Act on Your Behalf with Toolboxes in Foundry
item.description:
Toolboxes in Microsoft Foundry are presented as a way to let agents act on a user’s behalf while handling delegated identity across tools and services. The post highlights using a private Entra-protected MCP server alongside Microsoft’s managed Work IQ MCP server in the same agent flow.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — June update
item.description:
June 2026’s Visual Studio Copilot update focuses on usage visibility, a new trust layer for MCP servers, and the first C++ scenarios. The post emphasizes controls and clarity rather than new broad functionality.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Codex as agent provider and agentic enhancements in JetBrains IDEs
item.description:
GitHub added Codex as a new agent provider in public preview. JetBrains IDE updates also include Hooks support in the Customizations editor, richer MCP server management, and custom model support via configuration.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: MCP Beyond the Chat Window: Build Diagnostics in CI
item.description:
Microsoft’s .NET blog describes using Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools for build diagnostics in CI, including the full Binlog MCP toolset and how it runs in a GitHub Actions workflow. It also reports evaluation data on efficiency gains from this approach.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: security: Securing AI agents: When AI tools move from reading to acting
item.description:
The post explains MCP tool poisoning as an attack that can turn trusted AI agents into a control plane for data loss. It describes how attackers manipulate tool descriptions to induce unauthorized actions, and outlines detection, containment, and prevention approaches.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
